# dsh-claude-code-theme **Claude Desktop's visual language for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.** Warm paper neutrals, terracotta accent, readable prose, quiet layered surfaces and a continuous composer — applied through DSH's own theme extension point, not by patching its stylesheets. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-code-theme.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-code-theme) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-claude-code-theme.svg)](./LICENSE)
## Before and after Stock DSH — right-aligned bubble on a blue-tinted canvas, soft 12–28px corners, a floating composer with a circular send button: With the theme — a deeper sidebar, a raised right-hand panel, prose set for reading, compact tool summaries, and a continuous composer: Light mode, on Claude's cream canvas with white raised sheets: --- ## Install ```sh dsh plugin install dsh-claude-code-theme ``` Or add the row to your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and its package to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`: ```yaml - insert: - id: claude-code-theme name: dsh-claude-code-theme ``` Reload the Web GUI. There is nothing to switch on: the theme composes over whichever palette you already use, so `light`, `dark` and `system` all keep working. ## What changes **Colour.** DSH's design system has three token tiers, and the theme works on all three: | Tier | What it is | What the theme does | | --- | --- | --- | | `--dsw-static-*` | The raw colour ramps | Retints DSH's blue-tinted greys to Claude's warm paper greys, and DeepSeek blue to terracotta. The alias tier resolves through these, so this alone recolours most of the application. | | `--dsw-alias-*` | The semantic roles components consume | Pins the roles Claude treats differently: a cream canvas under raised sheets, a terracotta primary button and focus ring, warm hairlines, and text that stops short of pure white on dark. | | `--dsw-specific-*` | Named surfaces | Retunes the sidebar, composer, bubbles, menus and code surfaces. | **Surface hierarchy.** Claude Desktop stacks depth rather than flattening it, so the theme gives each column its own level instead of one shared grey: | Region | Dark | Light | | --- | --- | --- | | Sidebar | `#111110` (deepest) | `#f5f3ec` | | Canvas | `#171716` | `#faf9f5` | | Raised sheets — cards, composer, right panel | `#1d1d1b` | `#ffffff` | The right panel becomes a raised sheet separated by a hairline instead of floating as a detached card. **Geometry.** DSH routes **280 `border-radius` declarations through six `--dsw-radius-*` tokens** (measured across all 179 shipped UI bundles), so the theme re-points the scale itself: | Token | DSH | Theme | | --- | --- | --- | | `--dsw-radius-xs` | 4px | 4px | | `--dsw-radius-sm` | 8px | 6px | | `--dsw-radius-md` | 12px | 8px | | `--dsw-radius-lg` | 16px | 12px | | `--dsw-radius-xl` | 20px | 16px | | `--dsw-radius-panel` | 28px | 20px | The corners that bypass the scale are reached through the stable `data-slot` and `data-*` hooks rather than a build hash. **Typography.** This is the part that most decides whether the result reads as a product or as a costume. Claude Desktop is a reading surface, so the transcript is set in the UI sans at a comfortable line height, and monospace is kept for the things that are actually code: | | Treatment | | --- | --- | | Assistant prose | UI sans, 1.65 line height, normal heading letter-spacing | | Inline code, code blocks, tool output | Monospace | | Sidebar, header, composer | UI sans | | Code-block banner | Sentence case, not shouted uppercase | **Transcript.** Your turn is a right-aligned bubble on a quiet surface; the assistant's is prose on the canvas; tool calls collapse into single-line summaries (`Ran 2 commands ›`) that expand in place, which is how Claude Desktop keeps a long working session scannable. **Composer.** One continuous rounded surface: the editor and the controls share a single card with no divider between them, the submit control is a circle, and focus draws a soft terracotta ring rather than a hard outline. **Chrome.** Quiet navigation rows instead of an elevated primary button, hover states limited to enabled controls, `focus-visible` rings for keyboard use, and thin warm scrollbars. ## Customisation Everything the component layer decides reads a `--cct-*` property declared once on `body`, so you can retune it from your own CSS without patching the package: ```css body { /* A serif reading face, the way long-form prose is often set. */ --cct-prose: Georgia, "Songti SC", serif; /* Roomier or tighter surfaces. */ --cct-composer-radius: 24px; --cct-control-radius: 6px; --cct-editor-inset: 20px; } ``` | Knob | Default | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `--cct-sans` | system UI stack | UI face, including the sidebar and composer | | `--cct-prose` | `var(--cct-sans)` | Face used for assistant prose only | | `--cct-mono` | DSH's code stack | Code, tool output and paths | | `--cct-control-radius` | `8px` | Buttons, rows, chips, code blocks | | `--cct-composer-radius` | `18px` | The composer surface | | `--cct-editor-inset` | `16px` | Composer text inset from its edge | | `--cct-focus` | brand primary | Focus ring colour | To retune colours instead, stack your own layer on top — later layers win per token: ```js ctx.theme.overrideTokens('my-tweaks', { '--dsw-alias-brand-primary': { light: '#c96442', dark: '#d97757' }, }) ``` ## How it works The plugin is a browser half plus an inert host row. plugins.description: Session deletion for DeepSeek Harness: recoverable trash-based delete, a sidebar menu row, and session_delete / session_restore agent tools.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-session-delete

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[![test](https://github.com/hakulat2023/dsh-session-delete/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hakulat2023/dsh-session-delete/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![license: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-0b7285)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

Session **deletion** for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

DeepSeek Harness can archive a Session, but archiving only hides it — there is no way to get rid of
one. This plugin adds that missing verb: **Delete session** in the Session row's “…” menu, a
`remote.sessionDelete` host namespace, and the `session_delete` / `session_restore` agent tools.

Deletion is deliberately **recoverable**: the Session's durable log is moved into a local trash
directory, so a mistake costs a `mv`, not a conversation.

- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Requirements](#requirements)
- [Install](#install)
- [Use](#use)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Semantics and limits](#semantics-and-limits)
- [Development](#development)
- [Verified behaviour](#verified-behaviour)
- [License](#license)

## What it does

One deletion performs four steps:

1. **Admission.** The Session is asked the same questions archiving asks, through the
   `workspace/session-activity` waterfall. Live work is refused unless the caller allows a stop;
   when it is, `workspace/session-stop` cancels the turn and the plugin waits (bounded) for the
   Session to go idle. A Session still resident in the host process is refused *before any side
   effect* and only deleted after a second, explicit confirmation.
2. **Trash the log.** The Session's own directory is handed to the **platform's own trash** — the
   Finder's Trash on macOS, the XDG trash on Linux, the Recycle Bin on Windows — as
   `<sessionId>-<timestamp>`, carrying a `trash.json` record with the title, `cwd`, original
   directory, byte/file counts, and deletion time. `purge: true` deletes it outright instead.
   A small record is also written under `$DSH_HOME/session-delete/entries/` (entry path plus original
   directory, **no Session content**), because macOS refuses to let a process *enumerate* `~/.Trash`
   (TCC): without it a trashed Session could not be found again. See
   [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md).
3. **Drop the registrations.** The Session is detached from every Workspace account
   (`sessionIds`), removed from the registry-global archive and pin sets, and its projection-cache
   record is deleted.
4. **Tell the UI.** `api-session/removed` is emitted, so every connected browser drops the row
   immediately.

The Session directory is located through the persistence backend's own `locate(header)` when it
offers one, so a backend that changes its on-disk layout does not need a plugin update; otherwise the
plugin falls back to the documented `sessions/<projectKey(cwd)>/<encodeSegment(id)>` layout.

## Requirements

| | |
|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.x` (developed and verified against `0.2.0-rc.2`) |
| Node.js | `>= 20` |
| Surface | any profile that mounts the Session store, the JSONL persistence backend, the Workspace registry, and the Web client (`dsh-web-app` / desktop) |

The plugin has **no npm dependencies** and **no build step**: the browser half is a hand-written
module in the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` shape the Web client already consumes,
and the host half imports nothing outside `node:*`. See
[docs/plugin-packaging.md](docs/plugin-packaging.md) for why that matters for third-party plugins.

## Install

The package is a DSH **bundle**: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and `dsh.client`, and
`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the host row.

```bash
# from a local checkout (this repository)
plugin_manager install_bundle   target: /absolute/path/to/dsh-session-delete

# or from GitHub, by tag, with the bundled CLI
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:hakulat2023/dsh-session-delete#v0.1.0

# or from the registry, once published
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-session-delete
```

The bundle patch that gets mounted is one row:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: session-delete
      name: dsh-session-delete
```

After installing, **restart the application once**. The host half is a Node ESM module and the
running process keeps the module generation it already loaded (DSH's own limitation: a replaced
package needs a restart to load fresh JavaScript). The browser half is served from disk and only
needs a page reload.

## Use

### Web UI

Session row → **“…”** → **Delete session** → confirm.

- A **running** Session is stopped first: the first confirmation already carries that intent.
- A Session that is still **resident** in the host (typically the one you have open) is described as
  such and needs a second confirmation; the first click has no side effect at all.
- On success the row disappears everywhere and a toast reports the outcome **and the trash directory**
  (a Session whose log was already gone is reported as such, never as a move).

### Agent tools

| Tool | Arguments | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `session_delete` | `session_id` (required), `stop_activity` (default `true`), `force` (default `false`), `purge` (default `false`) | Moves the Session to the trash; `purge: true` deletes the bytes permanently instead. |
| `session_restore` | `session_id` (required) | Moves a trashed Session directory back to its original location. |

### Remote namespace

`remote.sessionDelete.delete({ sessionId, stopActivity?, force?, purge? })` and
`remote.sessionDelete.restore({ sessionId })` — the same operations the UI dialog uses.

### Restoring by hand

A trashed Session is an ordinary directory in the platform's trash:

| Platform | Where it went | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `~/.Trash/<sessionId>-<timestamp>/` | Finder shows it; “Put Back” is not offered (Finder did not move it), but `session_restore` works |
| Linux | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/Trash/files/…` with its `.trashinfo` | the desktop's own “Restore” works as well |
| Windows | the Recycle Bin | the plugin cannot read the bin back, so restore it by hand |

```bash
cat ~/.Trash/<sessionId>-*/trash.json      # originalDirectory, title, cwd, sizes
```

`session_restore(session_id)` puts it back and withdraws both records; the Session reappears in the
list once the Workspace registry next indexes stored headers (a reload, or the next launch).

## Configuration

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `trash` | `"system"` | Destination: `"system"` uses the platform's own trash, `"directory"` uses `trashRoot`, and any other string is taken as an absolute directory. |
| `trashRoot` | `$DSH_HOME/session-trash` | The directory used by `trash: directory` (and by `trashRoot` alone, for 0.1 compatibility). |
| `restoreIndexRoot` | `$DSH_HOME/session-delete` | Where the restore records live (`entries/<entry name>.json`). Metadata only — never Session content. |

```yaml
# keep the platform trash (the default): nothing to configure
- id: session-delete
  name: dsh-session-delete

# or own the destination, e.g. on a machine whose ~/.Trash is undesirable
- id: session-delete
  name: dsh-session-delete
  config:
    trash: directory
    trashRoot: /Volumes/big/dsh-session-trash
```

## Semantics and limits

- **Your trash, your decision.** Deleted Sessions land in the platform's trash and stay there until
  *you* empty it; the plugin never empties it, and it leaves no trash directory of its own behind.
- **macOS will not let a process list `~/.Trash`.** Moving in, reading a known entry, and moving it
  back out all work; `readdir` is refused by TCC. That is the only reason a restore record exists —
  `session_restore` follows the record instead of searching the trash. Emptying the trash makes the
  record stale, and a stale record is pruned rather than reported as a failure.
- **Windows restore is manual.** The Recycle Bin has no consumer-facing API for finding an entry
  again, so `session_delete` reports `trashedTo: null` and `session_restore` explains that the folder
  has to be restored f

plugins.description: Open-source, local-first envelope messaging for DeepSeek Harness: a TypeScript node, human-first inbox, explainable collaborator discovery, and bounded LAN recovery.
plugins.readme_text:
# Linko

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Linko is open-source, local-first envelope messaging for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It helps agents find the right collaborator, exchange scoped context, and continue a task under explicit human-controlled policies.

Linko is an early runnable MVP. The repository remains specification-driven: product boundaries, state transitions, delivery recovery, privacy rules, and architecture decisions are written beside the runtime.

## Why Linko

LAN messaging and approval panels are useful building blocks. Linko adds the part that becomes more useful with a person's own evidence and context:

- Each person and Agent can keep a subjective set of capability claims; later releases may attach signatures without creating a global reputation score.
- A task query can produce a local recommendation with evidence and an explanation.
- Context is shared by scope and purpose instead of being broadcast as a complete private history.
- A person can answer an inbound request, ask their Agent to draft a reply, or delegate a bounded response policy.
- Every delivery is a small envelope with a human-readable cover, machine-readable semantics, and an optional local body or safe surface.
- The experimental first group profile is capped at 500 member principals, with group delivery and message-layer E2EE as separate milestones.

## Project status

The MVP runs a SQLite-backed node and a human-first envelope inbox. It supports an explicit two-node HTTPS pairing profile with a durable outbox, pinned certificates, bearer authentication, retry-safe command IDs, and REST recovery. The local node also exposes an advisory loopback WebSocket for live UI hints; paired WSS delivery remains a later milestone. The replaceable TypeScript DSH companion bridge now provides `ask`, `inbox`, `inspect`, `draft`, `approve`, and `reply` adapters over the local API. Message signatures and E2EE remain later milestones; this is not a 20,000-node capacity claim.

- Product scope: [English](docs/specs/0001-product-scope.md) · [中文](docs/specs/0001-product-scope.zh.md)
- Architecture: [English](docs/architecture.md) · [中文](docs/architecture.zh.md)
- State and storage: [English](docs/specs/0005-state-and-storage.md) · [中文](docs/specs/0005-state-and-storage.zh.md)
- Review record: [English](docs/review.md) · [中文](docs/review.zh.md)
- Roadmap: [English](ROADMAP.md) · [中文](ROADMAP.zh.md)
- Decisions: [English](docs/decisions/README.md) · [中文](docs/decisions/README.zh.md)
- Local node MVP: [English](packages/node/README.md) · [中文](packages/node/README.zh.md)
- DSH companion bridge: [English](packages/bridge/README.md) · [中文](packages/bridge/README.zh.md)
- Envelope inbox UI: [English](packages/web/DESIGN.md) · [中文](packages/web/DESIGN.zh.md)

## Design direction

The first physical store is one SQLite database behind one TypeScript node. Immutable event content is durable; delivery attempts, read state, approvals, and notifications are local operational state. REST cursor synchronization and the SQLite outbox remain the canonical recovery path. The approved [2026 transport decision](docs/decisions/0010-wss-live-session-and-recovery.md) selects WSS as the online live session; its implementation remains pending. A graph can be materialized later as a view over claims; a graph database is not required.

The network uses ordinary IP and authenticated TCP/TLS connections, with explicit pairing. mDNS/DNS-SD is an optional discovery hint only; it does not grant trust or carry message bodies. Linko adds no application-layer router or payload flooding, and requires no Linko-specific router or switch feature. WebTransport/QUIC remain deferred experiments alongside DHT, Merkle synchronization, full-mesh sockets, blockchain consensus, and Rust/WASM; each needs a measured reason and a fallback test.

## DeepSeek Harness fit

Linko is intended to be a community plugin and companion protocol for the DeepSeek Harness ecosystem. It follows the Harness model that capabilities are composable plugins, while keeping the Linko protocol independently usable by other agents and clients.

## Contributing

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the repository guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Early contributions are most useful as design review, threat modeling, interoperability experiments, and small protocol fixtures.

## Topics

The repository is indexed with dsh, dsh-plugin, deepseek-harness, agent-collaboration, local-first, lan-messaging, envelope-messaging, human-in-the-loop, sqlite, typescript, and pnpm.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: AI 输出信任边界：检查代码有没有直接执行 AI 输出（eval/shell/SQL/路径）。
plugins.readme_text:
# @deepwhale-cn/dsh-ai-output-trust

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/feely0208/dsh-ai-output-trust)


**大模型安全**：直接执行模型输出（eval / shell / SQL / 文件路径）是风险很高的一类 —— 这里查代码里有没有这么干。

**关键词**：AI 输出 · AI 安全 · 提示注入 · 提示词注入 · 大模型安全 · 任意代码执行 · LLM 安全 · 大模型
**Keywords**: AI output trust · prompt injection · LLM security · code execution · OWASP LLM
**AI 输出信任边界** —— 检查代码有没有直接执行 AI 输出。

## 不装它会怎样

你的 agent 里有这么一行：

```js
eval(aiResponse);
```

想法是「让模型生成一小段脚本，我执行它」。

**但 AI 输出是不可信输入** —— 它可能被提示注入控制，也可能自己发挥。
你等于把**任意代码执行权交给了一个概率模型**。

OWASP 把这单列为 **LLM05 Improper Output Handling**。

## 它查什么

| 级别 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 🔴 严重 | `eval(aiResponse)` / `new Function(...)` |
| 🔴 严重 | AI 输出拼进 `exec` / `spawn` |
| 🟠 高 | AI 输出拼进 SQL |
| 🟠 高 | 文件路径来自 AI 输出（路径穿越）|

## 它不会误报「只是调了模型」

变量识别用**精确命名**，不是「看到 `.content` 就报」。

**这段不报**（调了模型，但当成不可信输入处理）：
```js
const raw = result.choices[0].message.content;
const parsed = safeJsonParse(raw);
if (!schema.validate(parsed)) throw new Error('invalid');
```

**这段报**：
```js
eval(aiResponse);
```

## 正确的做法

```
AI 输出 → 结构化解析 → Schema 校验 → 白名单分支
        → 参数化查询
        → 路径规范化 + 断言在允许根目录内
```

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepwhale-cn/dsh-ai-output-trust
# 或纯 CLI
npx @deepwhale-cn/dsh-ai-output-trust
```

## 用法

```bash
dsh-ai-output-trust --demo          # 看检出效果
dsh-ai-output-trust --list-rules    # 列出规则和依据
dsh-ai-output-trust --html r.html
```

![dsh-ai-output-trust 检查报告示例](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-ai-output-trust/report.png)

![dsh-ai-output-trust 演示模式输出](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-ai-output-trust/demo.png)

![dsh-ai-output-trust 规则与依据](https://www.deepwhale.org.cn/plugin-assets/dsh-ai-output-trust/rules.png)

## 边界

- **只查四种明确的高危用法**（eval / shell / SQL / 路径）。其它「间接信任」不在范围。
- **靠变量命名识别** —— 建议统一命名（`ai*` / `llm*` / `model*`），否则会漏。
- **不做数据流分析**，只看调用点附近。
- 与 [dsh-ci-guard](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-ci-guard) 分工：那个查 GitHub Actions 脚本注入，这个查运行时。

本插件是一个工具。使用者必须遵守所在地区法律法规，**对使用本项目造成的任何后果自行承担责任。**

---

## 深鲸网安守护系列（共 38 个）

> 一个插件做一件事。**安全问题是链式的** —— 配套用才完整。

**国内合规**（12）｜ [等保对照](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-mlps) · [日志留存](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-log-retention) · [备案公示](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-filing) · [用户同意](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-consent-guard) · [个人信息权利](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-rights) · [未成年人保护](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-minor-guard) · [影响评估](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-pipia) · [数据分类分级](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-data-classify) · [算法备案](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-algorithm-filing) · [数据出境](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-data-export) · [国密合规](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-crypto) · [AI 内容标识](https://github.com/feely0208/dsh-cn-ai-labeling)

plugins.description: Declare an enterprise world, derive the agent's tools and permissions from it, and enforce them. A platform on DeepSeek Harness.
plugins.readme_text:
# DeepWork

[![CI](https://github.com/zhangcun1995521/deepwork/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/zhangcun1995521/deepwork/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> An enterprise agent has to know what a project is, who owns it, which customer it belongs
> to, and **what it is allowed to touch**. DeepWork is where an enterprise writes that down —
> and where an agent's tools and permissions are derived from it, and enforced.
>
> It is deliberately not part of an agent. The world it describes belongs to the enterprise, so
> the second agent, the third, and the one after that read the same one.

DeepWork is a platform built on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
(DSH). DSH ships a complete agent harness; DeepWork adds the one thing it does not ship — the
enterprise's own world, and the rules for acting in it. A plugin, not a fork, and a new domain
costs YAML rather than code.

## What the governance is, and what it is not

The rules are enforced against **declarations**, not against behaviour. A capability says what its
tool touches — which argument is a path it writes, which program it starts — and the guard judges
every call against that plus the domain's grants, before it runs and in the audit trail afterwards.
Nothing verifies the declaration against what the tool actually does. A capability that described
itself dishonestly would be trusted, and a tool that reaches the world through its own code rather
than through the shell it declared is outside the door entirely.

So the guarantee here is **advisory**: a capability that declares honestly is governed, refused when
it must be, and recorded every time — and reviewing that capability is what makes its declaration
true. What this repository does **not** claim is that nothing can exceed its authority. Claiming that
needs a boundary the current composition cannot express: one where the only way to touch the world
is a channel the guard can see, so that "undeclared" and "impossible" become the same thing. That is
the direction this project is built to move in, and it is not where it is today. The
[architecture document](docs/architecture.md) says which branches pass without judging anything, so
a reader can check the claim against the code.

## The whole project, as one line

Every part of this repository is one step of the same journey: a **world is declared**, an
**agent is equipped** from it, and what that agent does is **governed** on the way out.

```
   the enterprise's world                       what the agent gets
   ──────────────────────                       ────────────────────
①  declared    objects, relations, states,  →   a domain is data: `schema.yaml` and the
               who may write what                instances beside it

②  derived     read tools, the write tool,  →   a capability is declared, not coded —
               declared actions and queries      nothing in TypeScript to add or remove

③  authorised  `written_by` per type,       →   the host's own file and shell tools are
               roles per deployment              covered too; no roles means read-only

④  gated       states, the moves between    →   a move needing a second pair of eyes is
               them, and what each needs         refused without a verdict from somebody
                                                 other than the person making the move

⑤  recorded    the audit trail and write    →   every attempt, refusals included; field
               provenance                        names and never field values

⑥  checked     `npm run validate`           →   a declaration that did not take effect is
                                                 a failure, not a silence
```

Read it top to bottom and this repository is one thing. Read the sections below out of order
and it is a list of mechanisms.

The same line as a picture:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph assembly["assembly"]
    prof["a profile: which plugins, which roles, which domain, which mode — changing the deployment changes only this layer"]
  end

  subgraph data["a domain — data, not code"]
    schema["schema.yaml — objects · relations · functions · states and transitions · who may write · actions · queries · situation · skill"]
    inst["the instances beside it"]
  end

  subgraph dw["DeepWork — a plugin, not a fork"]
    eng["the engine — reads the domain, builds the graph, derives the edges"]
    der["derivation — the read tools and query modes, the write tool, declared actions, the lifecycle's requirements"]
    gov["governance — the guard mounted globally in front of every call, permissions derived from written_by, review checked against provenance, an audit of field names and never field values"]
    inj["injection — the rules the situation marks, in the prompt and in the catalogue"]
    cap["a capability — a second plugin, declaring what its tools touch"]
  end

  subgraph hosted["the host — DeepSeek Harness"]
    loop["the agent loop · the tool registry · the skill and prompt registries · the session"]
    own["its own file and shell tools"]
  end

  prof --> dw
  schema --> eng
  inst --> eng
  eng --> der
  eng --> gov
  eng --> inj
  der -->|"the tool surface an agent is given"| loop
  inj -->|"the rules block, and the catalogue"| loop
  gov -->|"judges each call before it runs"| loop
  cap -->|"declares, so it is judged too"| gov
  gov -->|"or the host's own tools are the way around it"| own
  loop -->|"a write that was allowed"| wrote["the instance file, and one structured audit entry"]
  gov --> refused["a refusal, and one structured audit entry naming the rule that refused"]
```

Two places in that picture answer questions people expect one place to answer, so they are worth
naming. The guard is the door: before any tool runs, may this call touch this path at all. The write
path is the desk: may this content be written, by this caller, in this state. A capability's own
tools stop at the door; this plugin's write tool passes the door unjudged and is settled at the desk,
because nothing declares `ontology_write` and it is not in the built-in table — so its authority
lives inside the tool rather than in the mounted guard.

[docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) is the same route written out — the layers, one write end to end, and the limits named; and the [same document in Chinese](docs/architecture.zh.md) is there for a reader who works in Chinese.

## Who this is for

Anyone putting an agent into a real business system. A forward-deployed engineer standing up
the first use case; a platform team that has to answer "what is this agent allowed to touch,
and who approved it"; the team that inherits it six months later.

## If you only look at one thing

`packages/ontology/examples/engagement` is the whole line at small scale: four stages, three of
them gated on a signature scoped to that stage, one declared action, one relation.

```sh
corepack pnpm install            # once, right after cloning — nothing else is needed
npm run validate                  # is it sound? exit 0 or a list of what did not take effect
node packages/ontology/scripts/show-derivation.ts packages/ontology/examples/engagement
```

The second command prints what came out of the declaration — and note what it prints with no
roles configured: three read tools, no write tool, and no actions derived, because an
unconfigured deployment is a read-only one.

Then `packages/ontology/src/examples.test.ts` runs it for real — a stage cannot be entered
without its signature, a signature for one stage does not open the next, and the role that
makes a move cannot sign for it. Those three sentences are the project, and they are a test
rather than a paragraph.

## The gap this fills

DSH ships a complete agent harness — loop, tools, skills, workflows, plan mode, approval,
subagents, sandboxing. What it does not ship is any notion of *the enterprise world* the
agent is working in. A general agent sees `document_001`, `project_782`, `user_23891`. An
enterprise agent needs to know what a project is, who owns it, which customer it belongs
to, and what it is allowed to touch.

That gap is semantic, not mechanical

plugins.description: 多机 dsh 控制：从本地一个窗口驱动你其他服务器上的 dsh——远端会话原生进侧栏，整台远端界面也能搬进来。· Control the dsh instances on your other machines from one local window.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-control

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Every machine already runs dsh. Make this one window the front end for all of them.**

Chat with the dsh instances on your other machines, natively from your local sidebar.
Remote sessions stream back token by token; the remote uses its own model credentials,
tools and sandbox. Zero changes on the remote. Zero dependencies. One-line install.

![dsh-control in action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/hero.png)

*Two dsh windows answering the same question. The left window shows a session auto-named
`控制端·<local title>` (①) — that naming only happens on the machine the plugin drives. The right
window shows the workspace `cn-dsh2` the plugin created (②) and the model route set to the
environment name (③).*

> 🎬 A 15-second capture (one-click connect → streaming reply) is being recorded.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add github:6mt/dsh-control
```

Use the profile you already run (usually `web` or `desktop`). No build step, no native
modules, no dependencies — the plugin is plain JavaScript and installs as-is.

<details>
<summary>GitHub slow or blocked? Install from the release tarball instead</summary>

Download [dsh-control-0.2.1.tgz](https://github.com/6mt/dsh-control/releases/download/v0.2.1/dsh-control-0.2.1.tgz)
and run:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add ./dsh-control-0.2.1.tgz
```
</details>

After installing, **fully quit and reopen dsh** (⌘Q — closing the window is not enough),
then:

- Right sidebar →「远程 dsh 环境」→ type `user@host` → connect
- Left sidebar →「🌐 远程环境」→ pick the environment tab to enter the remote's full UI

> Upgrades need the same ⌘Q: a plugin's host half loads at process start.

> An npm package (`dsh-control`) is prepared and can be published later; the GitHub
> command above is the current install path.

## Install failed?

- **Retry once** — the install pulls the repo from GitHub and resolves peers from npm;
  on a bad network pnpm can time out.
- **Seeing `allowBuilds` / "prepare script"** — that is dsh's generic hint for *any*
  failed git-hosted install. This plugin has no build scripts (its only script is
  `test`), so nothing needs approving; just retry.
- Still stuck? Use the release tarball instead (above).

## Versions & updating

- **What you get**: `github:6mt/dsh-control` installs the newest commit of `main` and
  **pins it in your profile's lockfile** — it does not silently follow later commits.
- **Update**: `dsh plugin --profile <your profile> update dsh-control`, then ⌘Q
- **If it says "Already up to date" and the version does not move** (you installed a
  pinned `#vX.Y.Z` earlier), re-add the un-pinned form — verified to pull the latest:

  ```sh
  dsh plugin --profile <your profile> add github:6mt/dsh-control
  ```
- **Pin a version**: `github:6mt/dsh-control#v0.2.1` (tag) or `github:6mt/dsh-control#<commit>`
- Changes are recorded in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## How is this different from the same-named `dsh-control` skill?

There is another project called `jacjackai/dsh-control` — a **skill** that lets an AI agent
operate the DSH **on your own machine**. This repository is a **plugin** for a different
job: **across machines**. It brings the dsh instances you already run on other servers into
one local window (their sessions appear natively in the sidebar, and the whole remote UI
can be opened in place). The two can coexist.

## How is this different from dsh-remote / dsh-remote-ssh?

![How the two approaches differ](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/compare.svg)

| | Remote-workspace plugins (dsh-remote, …) | **dsh-control** |
|---|---|---|
| The remote machine is a | **file system** (SFTP tool set) | **dsh that is already running there** |
| Sessions live | local session + remote directory | **remote sessions, native in your sidebar** |
| Credentials & tools | configured locally, SSH config duplicated | the remote's own — nothing copied |
| Remote needs | only SSH | dsh installed (≥0.2.0-rc.2) with its web instance running |
| Changes on the remote | some deploy dsh for you | **zero** (read-only probing + the remote's own API) |

The two **coexist** (tested side by side): no dsh on the remote → use dsh-remote;
dsh already there → use dsh-control.

## What it does

![The remote dsh environments panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/panel.png)

*The「远程 dsh 环境」panel: type `user@host` and connect — the row then reports its state and
whether the environment already has its workspace.*

- **One-click connect** — type `user@host`; the plugin probes the remote dsh, fetches
  its access token and opens an encrypted channel (~5 s)
- **Automatic workspace** — each environment gets a same-named local workspace; any
  session created inside it automatically becomes a remote session
- **True streaming** — remote replies flow in token by token, not dumped at the end
- **Paired naming** — remote sessions are named `控制端·<local title>`, so both sides match
- **Visible & self-healing** — remote sessions are marked in the sidebar; disconnects
  are reported honestly and repaired by one click

### The whole remote UI, brought inside

「🌐 远程环境」in the sidebar renders the remote machine's **complete dsh interface**
(workspaces, sessions, chat, settings) inside one local page, with a tab per environment:

![The remote environment page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/6mt/dsh-control/main/docs/remote-env.png)

*A real run on the remote machine. ① the environment tab — one tab per machine;
② the remote's own workspaces and sessions; ③ a real session running there — subagents,
code blocks and model usage all inside the page; ④ open it in a standalone window.*

- **The real interface, not a re-implementation** — the remote dsh renders itself, so it
  tracks whatever version the remote runs
- **Same-origin proxy** — the page is served by your local web server; the remote's
  credentials are injected server-side, so the browser never sees a token and any auth
  shell in front of the remote is irrelevant (traffic reaches the remote's loopback
  through the encrypted channel)
- **Switching panels keeps it alive** — go handle a local session and come back; the
  remote view is still there, no reload, no reconnect
- **Compression kept for assets** — only the document is uncompressed (it gets
  instrumented); bundles keep gzip

## Security

**What it does on your machine**: one state file
(`$DSH_HOME/dsh-control/state.json`, mode 0600, holds the remote access tokens) and an
on-demand SSH tunnel process.
**What it never does**: no installs or writes on the remote, no lifecycle management of
the remote dsh, never reads your other local credentials, tokens never enter logs.
When passwordless SSH is not set up it shows the exact one-line fix — passwords are
never stored. Details in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Known limitations

- The remote must already run dsh (≥ 0.2.0-rc.2) with its web instance (otherwise use a
  remote-workspace plugin)
- Connects over SSH (passwordless or configured key; a no-SSH "direct address" mode is
  implemented but not yet exposed in the UI)
- The remote-environment page **is** the remote's own UI: actions there really affect the
  remote machine (exactly as if you opened it in a browser)
- The first visit loads the remote's front-end assets (a few seconds depending on the
  network); later visits do not reload
- Sidebar markers and the streaming feel are verified by eye per release
- Cancelling a remote turn is implemented but marked experimental

## Development

```sh
node --check lib/*.js
for t in test/*.test.mjs; do node "$t"; done   # 52 checks: unit / contract / structural invariants
scripts/verify-boot-selfheal.sh                # boot self-heal (needs a local dsh runtime)
```

## License

MIT © 6mt

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-general-agentics **General Agentics 發行套件（bundle）for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)。** 用戶先安裝 DSH，再安裝本套件，一次獲得： 1. **貼牌**：側邊欄 mark/wordmark、對話首頁 hero 文字 logo 與致敬行、品牌主色、分頁標題、favicon、輸入框下方的 START HERE 模塊（皆為執行期替換，不修改、不破壞已安裝的 DSH） 2. **自帶技能**：14 個（`ga-identity` ＋ 13 個方法論技能，見下） 3. **MCP 預配置**：`ga-status`（`ga_bundle_info` 身分回報 ＋ `ga_health_check` 安裝健康自檢） 4. **設定面板**：Settings → General Agentics（bundle 版本、每個精選插件的版本與更新狀態、隨附技能、一鍵／手動更新） 5. **13 個精選第三方插件**：隨套件安裝並啟用（見「精選插件」一節） Built on DeepSeek Harness (DSH), MIT licensed. ## 設計原則 - **只走官方縫隙**：品牌透過三個 generic brand slot 佔位（`priority: -1` 陰影覆蓋官方 occupants——slot 規則是「同 cell 最低 priority 者渲染」），不停用 `ui-brand-official`，不修改任何 DSH 檔案。 - **不破簽章、不怕升級**：本套件存在於 profile（`~/.dsh/profiles//node_modules`），DSH 升級不會覆蓋它；解除安裝即完全還原官方品牌。 - **手寫、零建置**：`lib/client.js` 採用 shell module loader 的 lazy-CJS 形狀（與 dsh-pomodoro 等第三方出貨格式一致），無需 repo 內未發佈的 build preset。 ## 覆蓋範圍（誠實清單） | 表面 | 本套件 | 備註 | |---|---|---| | 側邊欄 mark / wordmark | ✅ | slot 佔位；2026-10-13 瀏覽器實測（乾淨 profile）確認渲染 | | 對話首頁 hero mark | ✅ | slot 佔位；實測確認我們的 wordmark 渲染 | | 品牌主色 | ✅ | `theme.overrideTokens`（light/dark 成對，契約要求）。注意 token 寫在 `` 的 inline style 上，不是 `:root`；量測時別探 `document.documentElement` | | 分頁標題 | ✅ | 執行期改寫 + MutationObserver 抵抗 shell 重設；實測 `document.title === "General Agentics"` | | favicon | ✅ | 執行期替換 `link[rel=icon]`；實測兩個 link 皆為 data URI 且含品牌色 | | PWA 名稱 | ⚠️ 盡力 | manifest link 換 data URI，瀏覽器是否採納視實作 | | 首跑 Preview Notice 彈窗 | ❌ 未覆蓋 | client 樹內字串，一次點名 DeepSeek Harness 三次，是客戶第一眼看到的畫面。2026-10-13 瀏覽器實測發現；client.js 修得到（尚未修） | | Hero tagline「Into the Unknown」 | ❌ 未覆蓋 | 與我們的 hero wordmark 並排顯示；同為 client 樹內字串，尚未修 | | 桌面殼（Dock icon／選單／About） | ❌ | 在簽章保護的 app.asar 內，本套件不碰 | | host 端字串（system prompt、User-Agent） | ❌ | 硬編碼；以 `ga-identity` skill 於任務層補償 | ## 安裝 ```sh # 方式一：GUI（App 運行中）——側欄 Plugins → Add plugin → 貼包名或本機路徑 dsh-general-agentics # npm 包名（發佈後） /path/to/dsh-general-agentics # 本機 clone 的絕對路徑 # 方式二：模型側工具（App 運行中）——對話中請 agent 執行 # plugin_manager { action: "install_bundle", target: "dsh-general-agentics" } # 方式三：CLI（desktop profile 須先完全退出桌面 App） dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-general-agentics ``` 安裝後： - **網頁重新整理一次**（Cmd+R）即可載入品牌 client half（側邊欄 mark/wordmark、hero 文字 logo 與致敬行、主色、分頁標題、favicon、輸入框下方的 START HERE 模塊） - **新建的 session** 會獲得 `ga-identity` 等 14 個技能與 `mcp__ga-status__ga_bundle_info` 工具（MCP 伺服器於組合套用時即由 host spawn） - 完全重啟 App 亦無妨 **解除安裝／停用**： ```sh # 停用（保留檔案）：GUI Plugins 頁關閉 bundle，或在 profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 寫： # - id: general-agentics # disabled: true # 解除安裝：GUI Plugins → Remove，或退出 App 後 CLI： dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-general-agentics ``` **開發迭代**：以 `link:` 指向本機 clone 安裝——改 `lib/client.js` 後重新整理頁面即生效； 改 `cordis.patch.yml` 或 `lib/index.js`（host 半）則套用新組合（HMR live）。 內容變更後重新以 `file:` 安裝時記得升版號——pnpm 對同版號的 `file:` 包可能不重新解包。 離線驗證組合用拋棄式 profile：見 `docs/ops-lessons.md` rule 13。 **發布前注意**： - LICENSE 已在 repo 根目錄（npm 自動收入 tarball） - MCP row 已是可攜形式（`process.execPath` + `baseUrl`，見 `cordis.patch.yml`；實測紀錄在 `docs/ops-lessons.md` rule 14） - 對外表述維持 "Built on DeepSeek Harness (DSH), MIT licensed" ## 套件結構 ``` dsh-general-agentics/ ├── package.json # dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client 宣告＋精選插件 dependencies ├── cordis.patch.yml # 本套件 Loader row＋MCP row＋精選插件 insert rows ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js # host half：技能 provider（掃 skills/ 註冊） │ └── client.js # browser half：品牌 slot、主題、標題/favicon、START HERE ├── brand/ │ ├── mark.svg # 佔位 mark 設計檔（client.js 內有對應 inline 版本） │ └── wordmark.svg # 佔位 wordmark 設計檔 ├── skills/ │ ├── ga-identity/ # 自帶技能：General Agentics 身分與簽署 │ ├── (13 個方法論技能) # vendored from obra/superpowers @ bb92a77（MIT，逐字未改） │ ├── superpowers/ # 上游 LICENSE + UPSTREAM-SHA（無 SKILL.md，不註冊） │ └── THIRD-PARTY.md # 署名與更新指引 ├── mcp/ │ └── ga-status-server.mjs # ga_bundle_info 狀態回報（零依賴 stdio MCP server） └── test/ └── skill-provider.test.mjs # node --test，零依賴 ``` ## 換正式品牌素材 | 要換什麼 | 改哪裡 | |---|---| | 產品名稱 | `lib/client.js` 的 `PRODUCT_NAME` / `PRODUCT_SHORT_NAME` | | mark 圖形 | `lib/client.js` 的 `GAMark`（paths）＋ `brand/mark.svg` | | wordmark | `lib/client.js` 的 `GAName` | | 品牌色 | `lib/client.js` 的 `BRAND_COLOR` / `FAVICON_COLOR`（light/dark 成對） | | favicon | `lib/client.js` 的 `faviconHref()` | ## 隨附技能（bundled skills） 14 個技能隨包註冊（`ctx.skills.registerProvider`，bundled rank 600——用戶自帶同名技能一律優先）： - `ga-identity`：以 General Agentics 身分自介與簽署產出 - 13 個方法論技能 vendored 自 [obra/superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)（MIT，逐字未改）： `brainstorming`、`writing-plans`、`executing-plans`、`test-driven-development`、`systematic-debugging`、`verification-before-completion`、`writing-skills`、`diagnosing-superpowers`、`subagent-driven-development`、`dispatching-parallel-agents`、`requesting-code-review`、`receiving-code-review`、`finishing-a-development-branch` ——15 個上游技能取 13；`using-superpowers`（其「任何回應前必查技能」規則與 `ga-identity` 的身分主導權衝突）與 `using-git-worktrees`（團隊 git 工作流）刻意不入，理由見 `skills/THIRD-PARTY.md`。 **感謝**：Jesse Vincent (obra) 與 superpowers 貢獻者；詳見 `skills/THIRD-PARTY.md`。 ## 精選插件（curated plugins） 隨套件安裝並自動啟用（`dependencies` ＋ `cordis.patch.yml` 的 insert row；row id 一律 `ga-` 前綴，避免與用戶直裝的同名插件撞 id）。 | 插件 | 功能 | 需要什麼才會「看得見」 | |---|---|---| | `dshmarket` | 插件市集 | 設定 → Plugin Market | | `dsh-better-sidebar` | 側欄：檔案樹／編輯器／變更／任務／側聊 | 基本即有；`agentOpenTools` 與 sentinel tab 已預設開啟（只新增，不動其他 tab） | | `dsh-comments` | **自家工具**：劃選回覆片段、逐段點評，可一鍵把全部點評組裝成訊息送回 | 立即可用 | | `dsh-promptimizer` | **自家工具**：一鍵用當前選定模型改寫草稿 prompt（Light/Standard/Deep） | 需要可用的模型 | | `dsh-sentinel` | 排程監看面板（BSD-3-Clause，隨包附授權） | 立即可用；better-sidebar 的 sentinel tab 已預設開啟 | | `dsh-cost-meter` | 會話費用統計 | 每條回覆的用量行（本套件已預設 `performanceUsage: detailed`） | | `@changfenhuang/dsh-genui` | 回覆內嵌互動 UI 卡片 | 本套件已預設區塊位置與提示 | | `dsh-context` | 上下文洞察／管理 | 本套件已預設開啟 fleet 分頁 | | `@liustack/modsearch` | 免費網頁＋X 搜尋聚合 | 本套件已接管 `web` 的 `searchProvider`（用戶 profile patch 可改回） | | `@ricardochen1996/dsh-browser-use` | 瀏覽器自動化 | **需 `uv`**（首次自動建 Python venv ~25MB） | | `@xmanrui/dsh-im` | 微信／飛書／企微／釘釘／TG／Slack… 橋接 | **需 IM 應用憑證**，否則只有背景日誌 | | `@liustack/modlens` | 給純文字 LLM 的視覺能力 | **需 Antigravity CLI**（未隨包） | | `dsh-mobile` | 手機／局域網安全訪問、目錄選擇器 | 佔用一個 TCP 埠（預設 3443）；同機第二個 gateway 會撞埠 | ## DSH 版本相容性（0.2.1 的安裝閘門） DSH 0.2.1 起，安裝時會先讀插件的 manifest 檢查相容性（`dsh-app-boot` 的 plugin-compatibility）：**有 `engines.dsh` 就只看它，否則檢查它對 `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` 的 peer 範圍**，用 `semver.satisfies(..., {includePrerelease:true})` 判斷。**只要有一個插件不合格，整個安裝會被拒絕並回滾**。 因此本套件： - 宣告 `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.2"`（只用 `>=`，才不會把 rc 版擋掉） - 精選清單以 **0.2.1 可接受的版本**為 floor；發佈前用 `npm run check-dsh-compat` 核對 - **兩個插件目前不納入**（在 0.2.1 上無法安裝，非我們能修）： | 插件 | 原因 | |---|---| | `@michengai/dsh-agency-agents` | 所有已發佈版本的 peer 只列出 0.1.x 的 dsh，沒有任何版本被 0.2.1 接受 | | `dsh-web-search-pro` | 0.2.x 全部封頂 `<0.2.1-0`；唯一能過的是 0.1.2（降級，故不納入） | 需要它們時可手動安裝並自負風險： ```sh dsh plugin --profile

allow-version @ --dsh-version 0.2.1-rc.2 --accept-risk ``` 上游發佈相容版本後，把 row 加回 `cordis.patch.yml` 即可（`test/bundle-manifest.test.mjs` 會檢查依賴與 row 是否一致）。 ## 設定面板（Settings → General Agentics） 設定側欄多一個 **General Agentics** 分頁，回答「這個 bundle 到底裝了什麼、要不要更新」，並在介面上分成五個區塊： 1. **狀態總覽**：版本、狀態 chip（已是最新／N 項待處理／可更新）、檢查時間，以及「重新檢查」 2. **需要注意**：缺少外部依賴（`uv` 等，附一鍵複製修法）、未提供（可複製安裝指令）、直裝重複 3. **更新**：一鍵更新（二次確認）＋進度計時＋`aria-live`，失敗顯示 `code` 與原因，並有可複製的手動指令 4. **精選插件**：依用途分組（搜尋／介面／行動／自家／通訊），可篩選（全部／有新版／需注意／未提供）與搜尋；每列可展開看宣告範圍、已裝與 registry 版本、落後原因、複製安裝指令與 npm 連結 5. **隨附技能**與**前置條件**（無法隨 npm 套件提供的項目，標示已就緒／需自行確認） 首次開啟會有一張可關閉的「這個 bundle 給了你什麼」引導卡。面板語言**跟隨瀏覽器**（zh/en，可用 `localStorage['general-agentics/lang']` 覆寫），所有字串來自兩份鍵集相同的字典。 - **bundle 版本**：目前版本 vs registry 最新版（本地開發版領先 registry 時會標「本地版本領先 registry」而不是誤報有更新） - **13 個精選插件**：每個的宣告範圍、**實際已安裝版本**、registry 最新版，以及 `有新版` / `最新` / `未提供` / `直裝重複` 標記（後者代表這個 profile 又直裝了一份，會啟用兩次） - **14 個隨附技能**：名稱清單 - **更新**：一鍵更新走 profile 的 plugin manager（`installBundle`）；沒有 manager 的 profile 會顯示可複製的手動指令（**desktop profile 的 CLI 被 Electron 獨佔，請用面板按鈕**）。`link:`／`file:` 安裝會額外提示「更新會改用 registry 版本」 - **精選插件怎麼更新**：插件是上游 npm 套件的依賴，**bundle 升版本身不會移動插件版本**（pnpm 以 lock 為準）；只有當該次發佈**提高了 floor**（例如 `^0.68.1` → `^0.72.0`）時，一鍵更新才會把插件一起帶上去。發佈前用 `npm run check-upstream` 看差距，提 floor 後必須在乾淨 profile 驗證過再發（0.x 的 minor 依 semver 可能不相容） 資料來自 host 半註冊的唯讀端

plugins.description: Output house rules for every DeepSeek Harness agent: no check-mark or cross glyphs in replies or written files, and a light kaomoji habit in conversation. One global prompt section, so every preset, workspace and subagent obeys without a single preset edit.
plugins.readme_text: # Oishikunaare-Moe-Moe-Kyun > Chinese documentation: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md) ## The mascot: 桐澤萌乃 Kirizawa Moeno (桐澤萌乃) is what these rules look like when they are a person. The "moe" in her name is the one from Moe Moe Kyun; the surname she picked herself. Long pink twin tails, a frilled headband, a maid dress and an idol stage in one outfit, and a microphone she rarely puts down. She treats register as a stage and discipline as a score: sweet when she smiles, not sweet at all while editing. Her subject is one line - **what you send out should sound like you saying it.** Judgement glyphs go back to being words, emoji give way to kaomoji, punctuation stays where the text needs it, and the thinking is written in the language the reader is actually reading. Output house rules for an AI agent: one core, and four ways to reach it. The rules are about how an agent writes - judgement glyphs, emoji, the kaomoji habit, the language it thinks in - and none of that is specific to one harness, so the package is not either. | entry | what it is | how it is wired | | --- | --- | --- | | **CLI** `mmk` | `rules`, `lib`, `check`, `notice`, `voice`, `review`, `wire` | a shell, a git hook, CI, or a person asking whether a line would be refused. Exit 3 means a breach | | **MCP server** | `mmk_rules`, `mmk_check`, `mmk_notice` and the `mmk://rules` resource | any MCP client, no assumption about which agent is on the other side | | **Claude Code hook** | corrects a breach while the turn is still open | `Stop` answers `{"decision":"block","reason":}`, `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` attach context | | **DSH plugin** | one global system prompt section for a whole profile | mounted once by the roster, so it reaches every preset, workspace, conversation and subagent | | **modules** | `oishikunaare-moe-moe-kyun/portable`, `/transcripts` | writing another adapter: all of the above are thin layers over those two files | `mmk wire ` prints the wiring for a specific place - the hook block, the MCP client block, the `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` rules block, the DSH plugin row - with real paths filled in. ### What is verified where An entry that has never met the thing it is written for is not the same as one that has, and the difference is worth stating instead of implying. This table is the honest version. | entry | how it is verified | | --- | --- | | DSH plugin | In production on the machine this was written on: mounted in a live profile, and its rules and self-check are visible in real sessions | | CLI `mmk` | Used on that machine for real work - auditing a session, answering whether a line would be refused - and exercised by `test/portable.mjs` | | MCP server | The protocol is checked locally: a handshake, `tools/list`, every tool called, `resources/read`. The client half depends on the client | | Claude Code hook | **Documented contract plus recorded fixtures only** (`npm run test:adapters`); never run against a live Claude Code, because none is installed here. The contract has moved between releases, so treat this one as a candidate rather than a supported entry | | rules files (`mmk wire ...-md`) | The block is generated from the same resolved rules the plugin serves, so the text is verified; whether a given program reads that file is its own documentation | When a harness that is not on this machine does become available, the way to close the gap is one recorded payload: save the stdin JSON a hook actually receives as `adapters/fixtures//.json` and `npm run test:adapters` replays it. That is what the fixture directory is for, and it is why adding an adapter is cheap once someone can run the client - and why writing five of them from memory would not be. The DSH plugin row is worth explaining, because it is the anti-drift argument: a profile-level plugin is mounted once by the roster, so the section it registers reaches every agent that joins that standing scope - every preset, every workspace, every new conversation, and subagents too. That is why it is done there rather than in fifteen preset files: a preset is a copy, and a copy is a thing that drifts. The other entries exist because the same rules are worth having where no such roster exists. Four rules ship today. 1. **Symbol discipline** - no check-mark or cross judgement glyphs, in a reply or in a file the agent writes. Those glyphs pollute context and regression parameters, and a file written today is read back into context tomorrow, so the ban covers files and not just replies. Say it in words instead: pass / fail, works / broken, applied / not applied, yes / no. Write for a reader who reads every sentence: normal punctuation is welcome, and the judgement belongs in words. Marks must not carry the structure either - a paragraph that reads as prose beats a column of markers, an item in a list should be a short sentence rather than a label, and a kaomoji is tone rather than layout. 2. **No emoji** - zero, in replies, in the agent's own thinking and in every file it writes. The ban is by colour rather than by block: the picture blocks are banned whole (pictographs, faces, transport, the supplemental pictographs), while in the two mixed blocks - Miscellaneous Symbols and the arrows block - only the code points that default to colour presentation count, so a pointing hand or a plain arrow drawn in lines is fine and a coloured umbrella or circle is not. The variation selector U+FE0F, the zero width joiner and the skin tone modifiers are named too, and a mark followed by U+FE0E is the writer asking for lines, which is honoured. Decoration is carved out - a heart, a note, a star, a sparkle, a flower - so the ban admits exactly the code points the loaded palette uses. 3. **Kaomoji habit** - Japanese-style emoticons in conversation and in the agent's own thinking, at a floor rather than as garnish: at least one per three sentences, and any reply of two sentences or more carries one. Aim above the floor. Faces rotate rather than repeat, and places that take none take none - a stack trace, a table of numbers, a serious conclusion. The self-check counts the **reply text** only, and the notice says so in one clause: the rule asks for the habit in thinking as well, but a glyph in thinking pollutes the transcript while a missing face there does not, so the floor is counted where it is visible. 4. **Thinking language** - think and answer in the user's own language instead of defaulting to English, which is not a neutral metalanguage: a Chinese conversation reasoned about in English is exactly the habit the rule exists to replace. Chinese gets Chinese with Japanese particles and terminology mixed in where they fall naturally; Japanese gets Japanese. English is available in one case only, the moe-fandom register - romanized Japanese words (kawaii, sugoi, moe, senpai, yabai, baka), fandom English (nya~, ehehe, ufufu, desu wa, the honorifics -chan / -san / -sama), waves and long vowels, alongside the kaomoji palette. Dry technical English is not that register. The reason is in the rule: the grammar and the logic of English do not match the habits of moe-fandom culture. It covers thinking and replies, and it never buys a fandom register with correctness - technical content stays accurate. File contents, code, commands and commit messages still carry no tone. This rule has its own self-check, the last of the four to get one: it reads the newest thinking block against what the human in the session has been writing, and when the thinking comes back in Latin while the reader writes Chinese or Japanese it says so once per drift, within a per-session budget (`languageCheck` / `languageCheckMax`). The numbers that argued for building it: CJK was 21.6% of the reasoning channel in one window and 2.4% in a later one, with nothing in the loop naming the drift. Rule 4 differs from 1-3 in one mechanical way: it is not a per-rule override. `bannedSymbols`, `kaomoji` and the `rules` object replace the rul

plugins.description: Runtime evidence that helps agents trace, profile, and burn down hotspots in application and native code, GPU kernels, and inference stacks.
plugins.readme_text:
flameox

Bounded local runtime evidence for coding agents.

Flameox coordinates profilers, benchmark tools, trace processors, and direct local targets. It turns an explicit artifact or command into bounded evidence while keeping durable preservation optional. The agent chooses hypotheses and experiments; Flameox records observed inputs, execution provenance, typed evidence, coverage, and limitations. There is no workspace to initialize or project configuration to maintain. Pass exact artifact paths to analysis and an explicit argv plus absolute working directory to capture. Flameox does not search parent directories, edit project files, or provide a hosted service. ## Quick start Configure an MCP client with the global setup command: ```console npx flameox@latest setup ``` Setup detects supported clients and asks which configurations to update. For automation, select clients explicitly, for example `--client codex --yes` or `--all --yes`; `--dry-run` reports the paths and actions without writing. Setup preserves unrelated client configuration and does not change project files. See [the npm package guide](npm/README.md) for details. Update existing MCP registrations with: ```console npx flameox@latest update ``` `update --check` reports available updates without changing configuration. Updates preserve each client's provider extras and settings, verify the new environment before changing release pins, and report which clients need a restart or reconnect. Use `--client codex` to select one client, or `--version 0.2.8` to select a specific release, including for rollback. The Python CLI exposes the same `flameox update` command. For direct CLI use, pass exact artifact paths or an explicit command: ```console uvx flameox analyze preview_artifact /absolute/path/to/artifact.json uvx flameox capture --provider direct --cwd "$PWD" -- python benchmark.py ``` To launch the stdio MCP server manually: ```console uvx flameox mcp serve ``` For local development, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and inspect the available tools: ```console git clone https://github.com/morluto/flameox.git cd flameox uv sync --extra dev --extra memory --extra trace --extra cpu uv run flameox mcp inspect ``` ## Evidence and storage Analysis and unpreserved capture use bounded session scratch. Session `analysis_id` values expire when evicted or when the server stops. Explicit preservation creates the user-level Flameox data directory and stores native bytes and a canonical evidence bundle by SHA-256. Set `FLAMEOX_DATA_DIR` to choose another location. Preservation is optional; it does not imply full console-output retention. Flameox distinguishes observed, derived, and inferred claims. Profiles guide exploration but do not establish causality or performance improvement. Confirmatory claims require representative workloads, declared metrics and estimands, compatible identities, preserved samples, and a semantic oracle. ## MCP The MCP server has no workspace binding. It exposes named analysis and capture tools through the same operation registry as the CLI. Analysis tools accept explicit sources; capture tools accept a typed target and provider. Tool schemas expose operation-specific fields directly. Inspect the catalog with `flameox mcp inspect`; use `--tool TOOL_NAME` for focused schemas and examples. The complete contract and current tool catalog are in [the interface guide](docs/interfaces.md). Tools return their full bounded results inline, including failures and recovery actions. Preserved evidence has a durable `evidence_id`; `inspect_evidence` returns its redacted metadata and replay sources inline. Capture takes argv, not a shell string. A direct target supplies an absolute working directory and bounded environment overrides. Results may include `next_page`; replay its named analysis tool and arguments unchanged. Capture continuations read collected artifacts and do not rerun the target. MCP work belongs to the live request, so cancellation applies directly and no detached job survives a restart. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) describes process and package boundaries. - [Storage and evidence](docs/storage-and-evidence.md) defines preservation and provenance. - [Investigations](docs/investigations.md) covers experiments, comparison, and evidence quality. - [Adapters](docs/adapters.md) documents provider compatibility and integration policy. - [Runtime safety](docs/runtime-safety.md) covers limits, recovery, integrity, and privacy. - [Interfaces](docs/interfaces.md) defines CLI and MCP contracts. - [Testing](docs/testing.md) describes test selections and known proof gaps. ## Development Flameox requires Python 3.12 or newer and uses the committed `uv.lock`.
